rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Hereafter, believers who had faith and did good deeds rejoice, while those denying God's revelations and the meeting with Him face punishment.
rows.anchor: The day when the Hereafter arrives, the believers and the disbelievers will be separated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage calls for glorifying God at evening and morning and praising Him at the stated times of day.
rows.anchor: when you enter evening and when you enter morning and praises are being sung to Him in the heavens

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif Lām Mīm is a complete sentence whose implied construction is Sūrah Alif Lām Mīm, the Qur'anic name of this sūrah.
rows.anchor: The implied construction is Sūrah Alif Lām Mīm.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching name signals that this sūrah and the previous one have little difference in their central themes.
rows.anchor: there is not much difference in the central themes of both sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sūrah clarifies the incident that disbelievers used to mock the promise of divine help, answers doubts among disbelievers and Muslims, and substantiates the previous sūrah's case for Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: this sūrah, substantiates and highlights the content of the previous one

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearby land in the prediction means Syria and Palestine, then adjacent to Arabia and ruled by Rome.
rows.anchor: Syria and Palestine which were immediately adjacent to Arabia.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persians took the Roman territories after internal strife in 614 CE, during Muhammad's sixth or seventh prophetic year.
rows.anchor: This incident took place in 614 AD.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive construction predicts that the defeated Romans will recover and defeat the Persians.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has predicted that though the Romans have been defeated yet this defeat is temporary

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍʿ sinīn confines the reversal to a few years, clarifying the near-future prediction as occurring before the decade ends.
rows.anchor: This made it evident that this revolution will spring before the next decade is over.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because idolaters used the Roman loss to support their worldview and distress Muslims, the emphatic forecast makes their joy short-lived and serves as evidence for Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters had presented this incident in support of the truthfulness of their thought and philosophy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: History fulfilled the prediction: nine years later Heraclius rebuilt Roman strength, defeated Persia, and recovered and expanded Roman territory.
rows.anchor: nine years after this incident Heraclius re-organized the Romans afresh and defeated the Persians

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Events in nations' lives occur by God's command, grounded in truth and justice, rather than by chance.
rows.anchor: Such great incidents in the life of nations do not take place by chance; they take place because of God’s directive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans' defeat resulted from corrupt collective character, since sound beliefs and rituals matter only when they produce proper conduct; reform would make them eligible for God's aid.
rows.anchor: the real thing is the individual and collective character which emanates from these beliefs and rituals or should emanate from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims rejoice both because the Romans are closer to them in religion and ideology and because the Qur'anic prediction supporting Muhammad's prophethood is fulfilled.
rows.anchor: a great prediction of the Qur’ān in favour of the prophethood of Muḥammad (sws) will be fulfilled

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim sympathy toward other nations increases with their closeness to Islam in beliefs, deeds, and ideology.
rows.anchor: the more a nation is closer to Islam in its beliefs, deeds and ideology the more sympathetic Muslims will feel towards it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can attach either to the Romans' coming victory or to the believers' joy; on the first reading, Roman dominance comes through God's help.
rows.anchor: The words ِ ّٰاللّٰہ ِر ۡصَنِب can be connected to َۙن ۡوُبِل ۡغَیَس or to َن ۡوُنِم ۡؤُمۡ الُحَرۡفَّی

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power makes His just will unstoppable, while His mercy means He does not arbitrarily pit nations against one another.
rows.anchor: since He is powerful, no one can stop Him in implementing His will and since He is merciful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording makes God's promise to help believers certain; people focused only on appearances fail to perceive its unseen fulfillment.
rows.anchor: This promise of God’s help is absolutely certain to materialize for the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes both the Romans' victory and the Prophet and Companions' victory over Quraysh, and the author points ahead to verses 47 and 60.
rows.anchor: The fulfillment of promise mentioned here does not merely refer to the triumph of the Romans but also refers to the triumph of the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those fixated on appearances cannot see who truly controls the world and consequently treat it as amusement.
rows.anchor: they regard this world to be a place of amusement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated subject emphasizes that idolaters are truly heedless of the Hereafter, despite not openly rejecting it.
rows.anchor: the repetition of the inchoative ( mubtadā’) evidences the fact that the Qur’ān wants to emphasize that it is these people who are actually heedless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabian idolaters' fabricated system of intercession and polytheism made their professed Hereafter belief meaningless.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters of Arabia would not openly refute the Hereafter; yet they had fabricated such a system of intercession and polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purposeful creation of the cosmos and its appointed duration imply that humans too have a purpose and must face judgment, reward, or punishment; the author connects the point to Āl-i ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah Āl-i ‘Imrān, precisely this topic is discussed thus:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom of creation is clear to those who search within themselves for truth, while blind followers, miracle-demanders, and disputants remain deprived of it.
rows.anchor: As for those who blindly follow others or demand miracles and signs to deny the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many foolish people imagine that worldly luxuries are for enjoyment until they simply perish, with no future accountability.
rows.anchor: they have been made to enjoy the luxuries of life and one day they will perish in this manner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remains of stronger and more culturally capable nations such as ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Midian show that messengers brought clear signs which their peoples rejected and mocked.
rows.anchor: nations of ‘Ād, the Thamūd and Madyan etc whose anecdotes have been mentioned in detail in the previous sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong those destroyed nations: their refusal brought just punishment, and their history teaches Quraysh that each person will answer for deeds.
rows.anchor: God was not unjust to them; they themselves were unjust to their souls.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse claims that God will recreate humanity and offers His initiation of creation as evidence for that claim.
rows.anchor: Found in these few words are both the claim and the evidence to this claim.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Re-creation is no harder than initial creation; indeed, repeating a task is easier, answering the deniers' claim that resurrection is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: repeating a task is easier than doing it for the first time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone returns to God alone, countering the polytheists' belief that they would return to favored deities who could intercede for them.
rows.anchor: Every one will return to God alone and no one else on that day will be there to which they will return.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yublis means to lose hope and become bewildered; the deities associated with God will not intercede for their worshippers.
rows.anchor: The word سلَااب means to lose hope and be bewildered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists who now unite in support of their deities will reject them on Judgment Day; the author says their stances shift across its phases, as discussed in Sūrah al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: I have explained in the exegesis of Sūrah al-Qaṣaṣ that in the various phases of the Day of Judgement the disbelievers will adopt different attitudes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic depictions often put future events in the past tense to present an event deniers deem unlikely as already accomplished.
rows.anchor: what they consider as improbable is presented before them by the speaker in the past tense as if the event has already taken place

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This life tests people by intermingling believers and disbelievers, often leaving the righteous oppressed and wrongdoers dominant; Judgment separates them.
rows.anchor: This world has been created as a place of trials and tests and hence believers and disbelievers are intermingled in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun rawḍa magnifies the Paradise garden, meaning the believers receive the grandest gardens.
rows.anchor: In other words, they will be in the grandest of the orchards of Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word yubrun means to make someone happy or blissful, and God will provide all that brings joy.
rows.anchor: The implication is that God will provide them with all the means that will make them joyous.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word muḥḍarūn conveys the wrongdoers' humiliation and helplessness as they are dragged to torment like convicted prisoners.
rows.anchor: they will be tied up and dragged towards the torment the way convicted prisoners are hauled up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to glorify God is presented as a requirement of belief in His oneness.
rows.anchor: This verse states what is required of people if they believe in God’s oneness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directly governs creation; all directives and outcomes return to Him, and He has no partner or intercessor.
rows.anchor: He is directly controlling it. All directives emanate from Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created humans with excellent qualities, but few use them well and remain thankful.
rows.anchor: He has created man with the best of qualities but very few benefit from these qualities and stay thankful to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject resurrection will find their confession useless; belief after seeing the realities would negate the purpose of intellect and moral awareness.
rows.anchor: a confession of sins by people will be of no avail to them on that day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers value truth, bow to Qur'anic verses, pray at night, and spend for God; their concealed reward contrasts with the unequal treatment of obedient and disobedient people.
rows.anchor: those who are devoid of arrogance and value the truth will profess faith in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received God's Book before Muhammad; as leadership came to steadfast Israelites, it will come to the Prophet's Companions if they adhere firmly to truth.
rows.anchor: in a similar manner He will bestow leadership on the companions of the Prophet (sws) if they strongly adhere to the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh mock the promised dominance and ask when it will arrive, but accepting it at that time will be useless; the Prophet should leave them to wait.
rows.anchor: professing faith in it will be of no avail to these people who are making fun of it today.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the previous sūrah, this sūrah's primary subject is God's oneness, with arguments, warnings to opponents, and glad tidings for steadfast believers.
rows.anchor: the primary subject of this sūrah also is tawḥīd.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation of the Arabic Qur'an was a great favour to the Arabs, yet they arrogantly reject it and demand the punishment it warns about.
rows.anchor: did a great favour to the Arabs when He revealed the Qur’ ān in Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a mortal messenger of tawḥīd, not God, and punishment lies outside his jurisdiction.
rows.anchor: as far as the punishment is concerned, this is not in his jurisdiction; he is a human being and not God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should repent and persevere and are promised eternal reward, while idolaters face doom for withholding charity and relying on alleged deities instead of fearing the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: The believers are urged to seek repentance and show perseverance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The organized world testifies to one powerful, wise, merciful God rather than a plaything or battleground of multiple gods; those distracted by alleged intercessors await doom.
rows.anchor: this world is not the product of a merry maker or the play field or battle field of various gods

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are warned by the destruction of ʿĀd and Thamūd, who rejected their messengers despite their nations' strength.
rows.anchor: Before them, the ‘ Ād and the Thamūd adopted a similar attitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, people's own body parts testify against them, no intercession helps, and their destruction is traced to thinking God did not know their deeds.
rows.anchor: their ears, eyes, hands and feet will bear witness against them and no one’s intercession will be of any avail to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguided leaders and followers are gathered in Hell, curse each other, and the masses ask to trample the leaders who misled them.
rows.anchor: the masses who had strayed from the right path will request God to show them those among the jinn and men who led them astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those steadfast on truth despite opposition receive the angels' glad tidings of God's mercy and favours.
rows.anchor: Those who adhered to the truth in spite of all the opposition and conspiracies will be given glad tidings of God’s mercy and favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet carries a noble call and should answer ignorant opposition with decency and forgiveness, a difficult but wise approach attained through patience.
rows.anchor: he should counter their ignorance with decency and forgiveness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan's hidden suggestions disrupt this patient response, the Prophet and Companions should immediately seek refuge in God.
rows.anchor: If any breach occurs in this attitude because of Satan’s latent suggestions, then immediately God’s refuge should be sought.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arguments from the surrounding world reinforce God's oneness and the Hereafter, and opposition to these clear signs is condemned.
rows.anchor: The argument stated in the beginning of the sūrah in favour of tawḥīd and the Hereafter is reinforced by certain other arguments found in the world around man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is God's great favour to Arabs; its majesty is affirmed, an objection fostered by People of the Book is answered, and rejecters' real ailment is exposed.
rows.anchor: Besides alluding to the majesty and exaltedness of the Qur’ān, an answer is given to an objection implanted in the minds of the idolaters by the People of the Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jewish objection asks why a new divine scripture was needed when the Qur'an acknowledges the Torah.
rows.anchor: when the Qur’ān acknowledges the Torah, what was the need of a new divine scripture?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People mocking the Hereafter because its arrival seems delayed, or because the Prophet cannot date it, are answered.
rows.anchor: People who were making fun of the Hereafter because it was not happening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear no Hereafter because of alleged deities are warned that those deities will disown them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: Those who had no fear of the Hereafter because of their alleged deities

none: Section heading and verse translation only; the translator notes that the author gives no commentary here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders and followers who unite against the Qur'an become enemies in Hell, where the masses ask God to show them their leaders so they can trample them.
rows.anchor: when they face the consequences of this attitude the leaders and followers will become blood-thirsty enemies of one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The steadfast who hold to God's oneness receive angelic glad tidings that their trial has ended and Paradise awaits.
rows.anchor: The angels of God will come to them with glad tidings that their period of trial is over.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should patiently forgive naïve opponents who disrupt the blessed message; this gracious response benefits his preaching.
rows.anchor: he should patiently forgive this misdemeanour. This gracious behaviour from him will bring great benefit and blessings to his preaching endeavour.
